segments.title: July
segments.clinicalNote: Stress hormone levels well within normal range (5.0–14.0 pg/mg). Good sleep patterns and steady energy.

segments.title: August
segments.clinicalNote: Sharp spike in stress hormone (>2.5x normal baseline). Triggered by intense workload, 23 evening calls, and cross-country travel.

segments.title: September
segments.clinicalNote: Stress hormone remains +42% higher than baseline. Although overall meetings dropped, late-night calls continued to delay recovery.

telemetry.triggerDetails: Baseline week: Regulated circadian alignment, stable restorative sleep.
Stable cadence: Standard quarterly planning load.
Moderate load: Early technical design sprints.
Initial climb: First cross-coast travel; minor sleep friction.
Pre-launch sprint: 6 evening calls past 8 PM; initial sleep drop.
Trigger: 44 hrs meetings + 9 late calls + SFO/LHR red-eye flight + 58% deep sleep drop.
Peak Crisis: 46.5 hrs load, 11 late calls, 4 timezone hops; Deep sleep crashed to 27 min.
Post-launch aftermath: High sympathetic tone and prolonged nocturnal cortisol elevation.
Meetings decreased by 30%, but post-7 PM Slack & email triage continued.
Sub-optimal recovery: Parasympathetic reactivation dampened by midnight screen exposure.
Gradual normalization, but allostatic set-point remains elevated at +49% baseline.
Current Scalp Root: 15.6 pg/mg. Stress levels remain elevated due to late-night calls delaying recovery.
